subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: What should OpenClaw's public web-tool egress boundary be for this request: a web_fetch-local hostname allowlist, a managed-proxy policy, or a cross-tool policy covering fetch/search/browser/provider fallback?
rationale: The request creates an operator-trusted security boundary and current related PRs encode different answers that automation should not choose without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Sponsor scoped web_fetch allowlist first
options.body: Review the narrow web_fetch hostname-allowlist path as an incremental first step, while keeping denied domains and search/proxy coverage as explicit follow-up work.

options.title: Make managed proxy the boundary
options.body: Pause local web_fetch config work and route application-owned egress policy through the managed proxy direction instead.

options.title: Require cross-tool design first
options.body: Hold implementation until a single policy covers fetch, search, browser, redirects, caches, provider fallback, and plugin HTTP behavior.

recommendation.title: Sponsor scoped web_fetch allowlist first
recommendation.body: Review the narrow web_fetch hostname-allowlist path as an incremental first step, while keeping denied domains and search/proxy coverage as explicit follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across SSRF, guarded fetch, docs, and web_fetch runtime surfaces involved in this boundary choice.
